CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female here for her annual visit. She reports struggling with depression on and off over the past year, particularly due to being isolated and working remotely. She is currently on Prozac 20 mg daily and feels the medication has helped her in the past. She believes increasing the dose may help her through this difficult period. She also reports chronic back pain that is worse with prolonged sitting at her desk at work but improves with movement and position changes. She experiences some numbing in her legs that resolves when she stands up or changes position, but denies tingling or pain down her legs and denies leg weakness. She is able to perform activities of daily living, exercise, and go to the store, though symptoms are bothersome with prolonged standing or sitting. She has a history of coronary artery bypass grafting performed at a young age for a congenital coronary artery anomaly. She reports her heart has been doing well and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies any distress. Denies tingling or pain down legs. Denies leg weakness. Acknowledges numbing sensation in legs with prolonged positioning. Denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Chronic back pain
Congenital coronary artery anomaly s/p coronary artery bypass grafting

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 mg daily
Aspirin 81 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works at a desk. Works remotely.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Does not appear in distress
Neck: No thyroid enlargement
Heart: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft
Back: Pain to palpation of lumbar spine, decreased flexion
Lower extremities: Good strength, no edema

RESULTS
EKG: Basically unchanged from last year
Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable from last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg daily, one tablet once daily
Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy; discussed pain medication as option but patient prefers to start with physical therapy
History of coronary artery bypass grafting: Continue aspirin 81 mg daily; order echocardiogram
